audit_objective: Reconcile why policy action recall diverges drastically from raw classifier recall

operational_definitions.Raw_Classifier_Detection: Model outputs a class label other than BENIGN (cls != 0)
operational_definitions.Composite_Label_Detection: Predictor outputs predictedClass other than BENIGN (includes 'Unknown')

friday_ddos.mechanism_explanation: DDoS LOIC generates massive packet bursts. Isolation Forest signals are active for 76.6% of flows, pushing 0.7*rf + 0.3*if >= 0.70 (MONITOR). However, 234 flows have low anomaly signals, yielding threatScore < 0.70, resulting in action=ALLOW.

friday_portscan.mechanism_explanation: PortScan reconnaissance packets look nearly identical in packet length and timing to normal connection attempts. Isolation Forest scores them as inliers (if_sig = 0.0). Because score = 0.7*rf_s + 0.3*0.0, the maximum possible threat score is 0.70 (at 100% RF confidence). 926 attack flows had threatScore < 0.70, resulting in action=ALLOW. Only 74 triggered MONITOR, and exactly 0 triggered BLOCK.

monday_pure_benign.mechanism_explanation: Although Isolation Forest flagged 1,328 benign flows as 'Unknown', threatScore was set to 0.55. Since 0.55 < MONITOR_THRESHOLD (0.70) and 0.55 < BLOCK_THRESHOLD (0.92), all 10,000 benign flows received action=ALLOW.

critical_governance_verdict: Zero policy false positives on benign traffic was achieved largely because the containment policy thresholds (0.70 for MONITOR, 0.92 for BLOCK) and the composite weighting (0.7*rf + 0.3*if) aggressively suppress threat scores to ALLOW. Consequently, the system allowed 92.6% of PortScan attacks and 23.4% of DDoS attacks to pass unmitigated. Zero false blocking is NOT proof of containment safety when policy recall drops to 7.4% on PortScan.
